source.title: Can LLMs facilitate interpretation of pre-trained language models?
source.authors: Basel Mousi; Nadir Durrani; Fahim Dalvi

record.tranche_reason: The study demonstrates concept labeling and neuron ranking, but does not test the claim versions about single-job neuron poles, explanation faithfulness on held-out activations, or attribution-graph sufficiency.
record.gate_note: The paper reports neuron-ranking overlap between broad POS concepts and selected sub-concepts. These results concern overlap in Probeless rankings, not whether neurons have one main job or whether explanations predict activations on new examples. Probe accuracies elsewhere in the paper measure concept decoding, not the claim's neuron-pole or explanation-faithfulness outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. ChatGPT labels clusters of contextual word representations, not individual neurons or neuron poles, and human raters judge label acceptability. Its neuron work only checks how much Probeless top-10 rankings overlap between broad POS concepts and their sub-concepts. No result shows neuron-level job shares (V1, V2), revisits InceptionV1 (V3), varies architecture or tools (V4), builds attribution graphs (V5), or checks explanations against held-out activations (V6, V7). The paper does not discuss or cite the original sources, so 'discusses' is the closest available relation.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is partly right but misses the main conclusion. The authors mainly conclude that ChatGPT gives accurate, semantically richer labels for latent concepts (clusters) than human annotation, and that these labels enable fine-grained probing and neuron analysis. The neuron-overlap result is a secondary demonstration.
record.recipe_differences: The study clusters contextualized representations, labels clusters with ChatGPT, and ranks neurons with Probeless; it does not use the original audit's pole-level labeling or held-out activation explanation tests.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that prompt design and adding context can change concept-label accuracy; it does not report these as changes to the neuron-overlap results.

fits_no_version.finding: In BERT-base-cased, human raters judged 90.7% of ChatGPT labels for latent representation clusters acceptable. Of those, 75.1% were rated precise. ChatGPT labels matched or beat human BCN labels in 75.5% of cases, and labeled 21 of 26 clusters that BCN annotators had called uninterpretable (Tables 1–2, Section 4.2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LLM-generated labels for clusters of contextual representations (not neurons) are judged acceptable by humans in about 90% of cases.

fits_no_version.finding: Probeless top-10 neuron overlap between broad POS super concepts and their sub-concepts averaged 0.36 (Adverbs), 0.28 (Nouns), 0.21 (Adjectives) and 0.23 (Numbers). Individual sub-concepts ranged from 0.0 to 0.6.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neurons ranked for a broad concept overlap only partly with neurons ranked for its fine-grained sub-concepts.

record.problems: The neuron results are ranking-overlap measurements rather than direct tests of a neuron's explanatory job or predictive accuracy. No control or uncertainty estimate for these overlap values is reported in the cited results.
record.rows_left_out: Appendix C Tables 11 and 12 contain further individual sub-concept and name-concept neuron-ranking scores. They are omitted because they are extensive concept-specific ranking results and do not measure any listed claim version. Probe accuracy results in Tables 4 and 7–10 are also omitted because they test concept decoding rather than neuron-pole interpretability or explanation faithfulness.

untested.parts: Share of Qwen3-32B neuron poles with one, two or no understood jobs; no neuron poles are labeled.
Neuron-level interpretability shares across models and scales. The five models studied are 12-layer encoders, and their clusters, not neurons, are labeled.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron and recursive generalization.
Effect of architecture, regularization or tool quality on the share of interpretable neurons.
Neuron-based attribution graphs and reconstruction error.
Whether explanations fitted to activating examples predict firing elsewhere.
Simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations on new text.

record.verdict_notes: The 90.7% acceptable-label figure resembles V1's ~90% share, but it concerns representation clusters judged by humans, not neuron poles, so it is not linked to any version. No uncertainty or controls are reported for the overlap values.

versions.untested_parts: The share of poles with one or two jobs and the share not understood.
Interpretability shares across models, architectures, and scales.
The InceptionV1 cat-and-car example and recursive generalization.
Architecture, regularization, tool quality, and the stated InceptionV1-sized-model estimates.
Attribution graphs, behavioral explanation, and reconstruction error.
Testing explanations on examples beyond those used to write them.
Automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.
